lines.name: Make complex data clear
lines.pitch: When your users are experts working with dense data, I design the views that make it readable at a glance. I did it for clinicians, with genomic viewers and visual variant analysis; for the International AIDS Society, with a world map of HIV cohorts; and first as a physicist, turning simulations into decisions.
lines.trace: SOPHiA GENETICS · International AIDS Society · Spie Batignolles

lines.name: Analytical reports & dashboards
lines.pitch: When decisions depend on scattered data, I build the dashboards that put it in one place: product, engineering and customer metrics that let a leadership team arbitrate quickly. Done for a clinical genomics platform, now with AI, and before that for telecom market analysts.

lines.name: Build the prototype, then scale it
lines.pitch: When an idea needs proof before a team commits to it, I build the first version myself, then lead the team that takes it to production. A multimodal prototype for oncologists and a gene/transcript viewer both went that way into a clinical platform; today my team tests ideas with users before development starts.

lines.name: Turn data into a product
lines.pitch: When your data could be a product in its own right, I help shape it: the data model, the concepts and the platform around them. With the CTO, I set a clinical genomics platform on that path, a direction the company still follows. Earlier, I built portfolio platforms for private banks and a production workflow for Swiss TV.
lines.trace: SOPHiA GENETICS · Odyssey Financial Technologies · RTS

lines.name: Scale a product & design team
lines.pitch: When your product team needs to grow, I have done it at every size, from 4 to 25 people: developers, Product Owners and UX/UI designers in one organisation. I led the one that took a new clinical web platform to the start of customer migration, and today I run a small team working as an R&D unit.

lines.name: Build products with AI inside
lines.pitch: When you want AI in a product where mistakes are costly, I design it so people can trust it: grounded in curated evidence, every citation checked, the expert making the final call. That is how my team built a generative-AI assistant for clinical variant interpretation, alongside internal AI tools for requirements and documentation.
